cornN.title: Corn nitrogen response
cornN.desc: Site-specific nitrogen dose-response curves, pairing canonical agronomic forms with statistical learning, plus an honest measure of how far each curve can be trusted. Separates site potential from response shape instead of black-box regression.

meandre.title: meandre
meandre.desc: Differentiable hydrology. Process-based catchment models written so every flux and storage term is differentiable, enabling gradient-based calibration at scale, identifiable sensitivity analysis, and hybrid models kept physical by conservation laws.

capillary.title: capyllary
capillary.desc: Differentiable constitutive laws for unsaturated hydromechanics. A pure Python library for coupled unsaturated flow, poromechanics, and contaminant transport, differentiable end to end for adjoint-based calibration, running in a marimo notebook with nothing to install.

tools.heading: The tangent/ suite
tools.intro: The work I'm proudest of: an open-source suite that makes scientific computing reproducible and install-free. Seven JavaScript modules, tested against the reference tools in R and Python. A data-science library, a Bayesian engine, and the note interface that ties them together.
tools.dsDesc: Data-science toolkit for JavaScript: ordination, clustering, classical stats and ML. The ergonomics of scikit-learn and the tidyverse, tested against both.
tools.notebookDesc: Local-first computational notebooks that run JavaScript in the browser via WebAssembly. No server, works offline, your files stay on your machine.
tools.mcDesc: Bayesian inference for JavaScript: probabilistic modeling and MCMC sampling in the browser, so a model can report how sure it is, not just what it predicts.
tools.suiteLink: Explore the full suite at suite.tangent.to

writing.heading: Notes on getting modeling right
writing.goblinTitle: How I killed my own model
writing.goblinDesc: I built an automatic mineral prospector, then tried to break it with strict space and time holdouts. It didn't survive, and that's the point. A look at why exploration data quietly teaches models the wrong thing, and how to catch it.
writing.more: More posts on reproducibility, differentiable modeling, and the capyllary build, as the work ships.

about.heading: Engineering rigor, natural-science context
about.body: I combine the precision of engineering and physics with the messy, nonlinear reality of agricultural, ecological, hydrological and geological systems. My through-line is reproducibility: models and tools that others can rerun, audit, and trust, whether a calibrated hydrological model for a government agency or a notebook that runs with nothing installed. Good science needs good tools, so I build both.
